text:
Samir: Heads-up — terraform apply for gpupool-module v3.2.0 failed during canary in us-east-1. Looks like KMS alias collision across accounts/regions.

Jess: Ugh. Error excerpt?

Samir:
```
Error: KMS alias 'alias/redwood-gpukms' already exists in us-east-1
  on modules/kms/main.tf line 23, in resource "aws_kms_alias" "gpukms":
  23: resource "aws_kms_alias" "gpukms" { ... }
```

Toni: I think the provider upgrade (AWS v4.x) changed alias import/create behavior. I bumped the module to use the new provider semantics in v3.2.0.

InfraBot: gitops-apply: PR #3822 apply failed (exit 1) — see pipeline logs: https://ci.redwood/3822/logs 

Maria: Can we short-circuit alias creation? e.g. module var enable_kms_alias = false as a temporary toggle?

Samir: We can't change the module API in a patch rollout without coordination. The canary must match the repo. Rolling the module version back in GitOps is the safest short-term.

Ryan: Alternative: import the existing alias into the canary state then re-run apply. Quick command: 
```
terraform import 'module.kms.aws_kms_alias.gpukms' alias/redwood-gpukms
```
but that requires auth to the target account/region and is manual.

Jess: If we do manual import, we should also add a post-apply check to ensure KV cache and node groups didn't get re-provisioned. Manual steps are error-prone for canary.

Toni: I'll open a hotfix that adds a conditional flag (retain_alias = true/false) and pins provider to 3.x semantics for a patch release. Won't change API but introduces a compatibility flag with default true.

Maria: Hotfix PR plus immediate rollback of the module bump in the env repo sounds right. Reverting the module version in the manifests will let the canary finish and buy time for the patch.

Samir: Agreed. Jess, can you revert the bump in the gitops repo and trigger canary? We need minimal blast radius — don't touch gpufleet sizing.

Jess: On it — creating revert PR now. cc @Toni for the hotfix branch.

InfraBot: gitops: Revert PR #3824 created by Jess — pipeline queued.

Ryan: Quick note — there are cross-region aliases in eu-west-1 that may conflict when we roll this out globally. We should run a discovery script to list alias ownership before reapplying. I can drop a script into infra-tools.

Toni: I'll include a migration runner in the hotfix that optionally auto-imports aliases when a flag is set. Won't enable by default.

Samir: Next steps: 1) Jess revert module bump (in progress) 2) Toni PR for compatibility flag + provider pin 3) Ryan run alias discovery and share results 4) Maria coordinate rollout window with SRE on-call.

Maria: I'll book a 30-min window and notify customer-facing teams.

InfraBot: gitops: Revert PR #3824 merged; canary apply started at 1912348000; monitoring.

Samir: Once canary stabilizes, let's merge the hotfix into main and then do a staged rollout with alias-import disabled by default. Also add a migration doc: how to import aliases and why the provider bump changes behavior.

Jess: Filed follow-up task in infra backlog: INFRA-2197 (add migration doc + discovery script + post-apply checklist).

Ryan: I'll start the alias discovery run and post results in this thread.

Toni: Hotfix PR #3831 opened — adds retain_alias flag and pins provider to 3.78. Will request review from Samir/Maria.

Samir: Thanks everyone. After we close this out, let's add an automated pre-apply check in our CI that warns on alias collisions for KMS resources.

Jess: +1 :thumbsup:

Maria: Noted — I'll add it to rollout runbook.

Samir: Closing thread when canary shows green and migration doc is merged.
